title: Joint species distribution models with imperfect detection in spOccupancy
text: vignette provides worked examples fitting joint species distribution models spOccupancy R package (Doser et al. 2021). Joint species distribution models (JSDMs) series regression-based approaches explicitly accommodate residual species correlations (Latimer et al. 2009; Ovaskainen, Hottola, Siitonen 2010). spOccupancy provides series functions account various combinations three major complexities often encountered multi-species detection-nondetection data: (1) residual species correlations (Ovaskainen, Hottola, Siitonen 2010), (2) imperfect detection (MacKenzie et al. 2002), (3) spatial autocorrelation (Finley, Banerjee, McRoberts 2009). vignette, provide step step examples fit following models: latent factor multi-species occupancy model using lfMsPGOcc() accommodates residual species correlations imperfect detection. spatial latent factor multi-species occupancy model using sfMsPGOcc() accommodates residual species correlations, imperfect detection, spatial autocorrelation. spatial latent factor joint species distribution model using sfJSDM() accommodates residual species correlations spatial autocorrelation. latent factor joint species distribution model using lfJSDM() accommodates residual species correlations. detailed vignette non-spatial spatial multi-species occupancy models account residual species correlations, see introductory spOccupancy vignette. models implemented spOccupancy, use Pólya-Gamma data augmentation computational efficiency (Polson, Scott, Windle 2013). provide brief description model, full statistical details provided Gibbs sampler implementations models Appendix S2. addition fitting model, show spOccupancy provides functionality posterior predictive checks Goodness Fit assessment, model comparison assessment using Widely Applicable Information Criterion (WAIC), k-fold cross-validation, --sample predictions using standard R helper functions (e.g., predict()). , first load spOccupancy package, coda package additional MCMC diagnostics, well stars ggplot2 packages create basic plots results. also set seed can reproduce results .

text: function simOcc() simulates single-species detection-nondetection data. simOcc() following arguments. J.x J.y indicate number spatial locations simulate data along horizontal vertical axis, respectively, J.x * J.y total number sites (.e., J). n.rep numeric vector length J indicates number replicates J sites. beta alpha numeric vectors containing intercept regression coefficient parameters occurrence detection portions occupancy model, respectively. psi.RE p.RE lists used specify random intercepts occurrence detection, respectively. specified want simulate data random intercepts. list comprised two tags: levels, vector specifies number levels random effect included model, sigma.sq.psi sigma.sq.p, specify variances random effects random effect included model. sp logical value indicating whether simulate data spatial Gaussian process. cov.model specifies covariance function used model spatial dependence structure, supported values exponential, matern, spherical, gaussian. Finally, sigma.sq spatial variance parameter, phi spatial range parameter, nu spatial smoothness parameter (applicable cov.model = 'matern'). simulate data across 225 sites 1-4 replicates given site, single covariate effect occurrence, single covariate effect detection, spatial autocorrelation following spherical correlation function, random intercept occurrence detection. occurrence random effect, assumed 20 levels variance 0.75. example, suppose levels corresponded different administrative units across 225 sites simulated, want account potential correlation sites within units. detection random effect, assumed 25 levels variance 1.1. example, suppose 25 different observers collected data, wanted account variation observer skill (thus detection probability) across different observers. Next, let’s explore simulated data bit move (plotting code adapted Hooten Hefley (2019)). simulated data object consists following objects: X (occurrence design matrix), X.p (detection design matrix), coords (spatial coordinates site), w (latent spatial process, psi (occurrence probability), z (latent occupancy status), y (detection-nondetection data, X.p.re (detection random effect levels site), X.re (occurrence random effect levels site), alpha.star (detection random effects level random effect), beta.star (occurrence random effects level random effect).  see clear variation occurrence probability across simulated spatial region. final step can fit model package data list use spOccupancy model fitting functions. requires creating list consists detection-nondetection data (y), occurrence covariates (occ.covs), detection covariates (det.covs), coordinates (coords). See introductory vignette details. One important thing note including random effects spOccupancy must supply random effects numeric values. Notice occ.factor.1 column occ.covs, random effect levels specified numeric value, indicates specific level random effect given site. spOccupancy return informative error supply random effects factors character vectors tell us convert numeric order fit model.

Detection-nondetection data y <- dat$y # Occurrence design matrix for fixed effects X <- dat$X # Detection design matrix for fixed effets X.p <- dat$X.p # Occurrence design matrix for random effects X.re <- dat$X.re # text: Let \(\boldsymbol{s}_j\) denote spatial coordinates site \(j\), \(j = 1, \dots, J\). define \(z(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) true presence (1) absence (0) site \(j\) spatial coordinates \(\boldsymbol{s}_j\). model \(z(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) \[\begin{equation}\label{z}     z(\boldsymbol{s}_j) \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\psi(\boldsymbol{s}_j)), \end{equation}\] \(\psi(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) occurrence probability site \(j\). model \(\psi(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) according \[\begin{equation}\label{psi}    \text{logit}(\psi(\boldsymbol{s}_j)) = \textbf{x}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\boldsymbol{\beta} + \tilde{\textbf{x}}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\textbf{w}(\boldsymbol{s}_j), \end{equation}\] \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) vector \(q\) regression coefficients (including intercept) describe non-spatial effects covariates \(\textbf{x}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\), \(\textbf{w}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) vector \(\tilde{q}\) spatially-varying effects covariates \(\tilde{\textbf{x}}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\). Note \(\tilde{\textbf{x}}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) may identical \(\textbf{x}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) covariates effects assumed vary spatially, subset \(\textbf{x}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) effects assumed constant across space. model reduces traditional single-species occupancy model covariate effects assumed constant across space spatial occupancy model (Johnson et al. 2013; Doser et al. 2022) intercept assumed vary across space. spatially-varying effects \(\textbf{w}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) serve local adjustments covariate effects site \(j\) overall non-spatial effects \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\), resulting covariate unique effect species occurrence site \(j\). Following Gelfand et al. (2003), model \(r = 1, \dots, \tilde{q}\) spatially-varying effect \(\text{w}_r(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) using zero-mean spatial Gaussian process. specifically, \[\begin{equation}\label{w}     \text{$\text{w}_r(\boldsymbol{s})$} \sim N(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{C}_r(\boldsymbol{s}, \boldsymbol{s}', \boldsymbol{\theta}_r)), \end{equation}\] \(\boldsymbol{C}_r(\boldsymbol{s}, \boldsymbol{s}', \boldsymbol{\theta}_r)\) \(J \times J\) covariance matrix function distances pair site coordinates \(\boldsymbol{s}\) \(\boldsymbol{s}'\) set parameters (\(\boldsymbol{\theta}_r\)) govern spatial process according spatial correlation function. associated software implementation  supports four correlation functions: exponential, spherical, Gaussian, Matern (Banerjee, Carlin, Gelfand 2003). exponential, spherical, Gaussian correlation functions, \(\boldsymbol{\theta}_r = \{\sigma^2_r, \phi_r\}\), \(\sigma^2_r\) spatial variance parameter \(\phi_r\) spatial decay parameter. Large values \(\sigma^2_r\) indicate large variation magnitude covariate effect across space, values \(\sigma^2_r\) close 0 suggests little spatial variability magnitude effect. \(\phi_r\) controls range spatial dependence covariate effect inversely related spatial range, \(\phi_r\) small, covariate effect larger range spatial dependence varies smoothly across space compared larger values \(\phi_r\). Matern correlation function additional smoothness parameter \(\nu_r\), provides flexibility smoothness decay spatial process. avoid computational burden associated fitting full Gaussian process model, use NNGPs computationally efficient statistically robust alternative (Datta et al. 2016). See supplemental material spOccupancy manuscript Datta et al. (2016) details NNGPs implementations occupancy models. account imperfect detection occupancy modeling framework (MacKenzie et al. 2002, @tyre2003improving), \(k = 1, \dots, K(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) sampling replicates obtained site \(j\). model observed detection (1) nondetection (0) study species site \(j\), denoted \(y_k(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\), conditional true latent occupancy process \(z(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) following \[\begin{equation}\label{yDet}         y_{k}(\boldsymbol{s}_j) \mid z(\boldsymbol{s}_j) \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_{k}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)z(\boldsymbol{s}_j)), \end{equation}\] \(p_k(\boldsymbol{s})\) probability detecting species site \(j\) replicate \(k\) given species truly present site. model detection probability function site /observation-level covariates according \[\begin{equation}\label{pDet}   \text{logit}(p_{k}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)) = \boldsymbol{v}_{k}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\boldsymbol{\alpha}, \end{equation}\] \(\boldsymbol{\alpha}\) vector regression coefficients (including intercept) describe effect site /observation covariates \(\boldsymbol{v}_{k}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) detection. complete Bayesian specification model, assign Gaussian priors non-spatial occurrence detection regression coefficients, inverse-Gamma uniform prior spatial variance parameters, uniform prior spatial decay (smoothness using Matern correlation function) parameters.

title: Spatially-varying coefficient models in spOccupancy
text: Let \(y_{k, t}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) denote detection nondetection species interest site \(j\) replicate survey \(k\) time period \(t\), \(t = 1, \dots, T\). model \(y_{k, t}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) conditional true occupancy status, \(z_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) species site \(j\) time \(t\) according \[\begin{equation}\label{zTime}     z_{t}(\boldsymbol{s}_j) \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\psi_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)), \end{equation}\] \(\psi_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) occurrence probability site \(j\) primary time period \(t\). model \(\psi_{t}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) following \[\begin{equation}\label{psiTime}   \text{logit}(\psi_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)) = \textbf{x}_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\boldsymbol{\beta} + \tilde{\textbf{x}}_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\textbf{w}(\boldsymbol{s}_j) + \eta_t, \end{equation}\] \(\eta_t\) random temporal effect parameters defined . Note covariates can now vary across space /time period. assume non-spatial (\(\boldsymbol{\beta})\) spatially-varying (\(\textbf{w}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\)) coefficients constant \(T\) primary time periods, represent average covariate effects across temporal extent data. model \(\eta_t\) either unstructured random effect (.e., \(\eta_t \sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma^2_{T})\)) using first-order autoregressive (.e., AR(1)) covariance structure estimate temporal variance parameter, \(\sigma^2_T\), temporal correlation parameter, \(\rho\). data \(y_{k, t}(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) modeled conditional true occupancy status \(z_t(\boldsymbol{s}_j)\) analogous SVC occupancy model, detection probability now allowed vary across site, replicates, /primary time periods.

text: spOccupancy fits single-species, multi-species, integrated spatial occupancy models using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). Models fit using Póly-Gamma data augmentation. Spatial models fit using either Gaussian processes Nearest Neighbor Gaussian Processes (NNGP) large spatial datasets. package provides functionality data integration multiple single-species occupancy data sets using joint likelihood framework. multi-species models, spOccupancy provides functions account residual species correlations joint species distribution model framework accounting imperfect detection. v0.4.0, spOccupancy provides functions multi-season (.e., spatio-temporal) single-species occupancy models. provide brief introduction package’s functionality, illustrate just one model fitting funcitons. information, see resources referenced bottom page.

what: Fit a spatial occupancy model using spPGOcc()
title: Single-Species, Multi-Species, and Integrated Spatial Occupancy Models
text: fit single-species spatial occupancy model BTBW data using Nearest Neighbor Gaussian Process. use default priors initial values occurrence (beta) regression (alpha) coefficients, spatial variance (sigma.sq), spatial range parameter (phi), spatial random effects (w), latent occurrence values (z). assume occurrence function linear quadratic elevation along spatial random intercept. model detection function linear quadratic day survey linear time day survey occurred. run model using Adaptive MCMC sampler target acceptance rate 0.43. run 3 chains model 10,000 iterations split 400 batches length 25. chain, discard first 6000 iterations burn-use thinning rate 4 resulting 3000 samples joint posterior. fit model using 5 nearest neighbors exponential correlation function. also specify k.fold argument perform 2-fold cross-validation fitting full model. Run ?spPGOcc detailed information function arguments. produce large output object, can use str() get overview ’s . use summary() function print concise informative summary model fit.

code: set.seed(400) J.x <- 10 J.y <- 10 J <- J.x * J.y n.rep <- rep(1, J) N <- 10 # Community-level covariate effects # Occurrence beta.mean <- c(0.2, 0.6, 1.5) p.occ <- length(beta.mean) tau.sq.beta <- c(0.6, 1.2, 1.7) # Detection # Fix this to be constant and really close to 1.  alpha.mean <- c(9) tau.sq.alpha <- c(0.05) p.det <- length(alpha.mean) # Random effects # Include a single random code: set.seed(400) J.x <- 8 J.y <- 8 J <- J.x * J.y n.rep <- sample(2:4, size = J, replace = TRUE) N <- 6 # Community-level covariate effects # Occurrence beta.mean <- c(0.2, 0.5) p.occ <- length(beta.mean) tau.sq.beta <- c(0.6, 0.3) # Detection alpha.mean <- c(0.5, 0.2, -0.1) tau.sq.alpha <- c(0.2, 0.3, 1) p.det <- length(alpha.mean) # Draw species-level effects from community means. beta <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = p.occ) alpha <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = p.det) for (i in 1:p.occ) {   beta[, i] <- rnorm(N, beta.mean[i], sqrt(tau.sq.beta[i])) } for (i in 1:p.det) {   alpha[, i] <- rnorm(N, alpha.mean[i], sqrt(tau.sq.alpha[i])) }  dat <- simMsOcc(J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, n.rep = n.rep, N = N, beta = beta, alpha = alpha,                 sp = FALSE) y <- dat$y X <- dat$X X.p <- dat$X.p # Package all data into a list occ.covs <- X[, 2, drop = FALSE] colnames(occ.covs) <- c('occ.cov') det.covs <- list(det.cov.1 = X.p[, , 2],                   det.cov.2 = X.p[, , 3]) data.list <- list(y = y,                    occ.covs = occ.covs,                   det.covs = det.covs)  # Occupancy initial values prior.list <- list(beta.comm.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),                     alpha.comm.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),                     tau.sq.beta.ig = list(a = 0.1, b = 0.1),                     tau.sq.alpha.ig = list(a = 0.1, b = 0.1)) # Initial values inits.list <- list(alpha.comm = 0,                     beta.comm = 0,                     beta = 0,                     alpha = 0,                    tau.sq.beta = 1,                     tau.sq.alpha = 1,                     z = apply(y, c(1, 2), max, na.rm = TRUE))  n.samples <- 3000 n.burn <- 2000 n.thin <- 1  out <- msPGOcc(occ.formula = ~ occ.cov,                 det.formula = ~ det.cov.1 + det.cov.2,                 data = data.list,                 inits = inits.list,                 n.samples = n.samples,                 priors = prior.list,                 n.omp.threads = 1,                 verbose = TRUE,                 n.report = 1000,                 n.burn = n.burn,                 n.thin = n.thin,                 n.chains = 1) #> ---------------------------------------- #> 	Preparing to run the model #> ---------------------------------------- #> ---------------------------------------- #> 	Model description #> ---------------------------------------- #> Multispecies Occupancy Model with Polya-Gamma latent #> variable fit with 64 sites and 6 species. #>  #> Samples per Chain: 3000  #> Burn-in: 2000  #> Thinning Rate: 1  #> Number of Chains: 1  #> Total Posterior matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = p.occ) alpha <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = p.det) for (i in 1:p.occ) {   beta[, i] <- rnorm(N, beta.mean[i], sqrt(tau.sq.beta[i])) } for (i in 1:p.det) {   alpha[, i] <- rnorm(N, alpha.mean[i], sqrt(tau.sq.alpha[i])) } alpha.true <- alpha n.factors <- 3 phi <- rep(3 / .7, n.factors) sigma.sq <- rep(2, n.factors) nu <- rep(2, n.factors)  dat <- simMsOcc(J.x = J.x, J.y code: set.seed(400)  # Simulate Data ----------------------------------------------------------- J.x <- 15 J.y <- 15 J.all <- J.x * J.y # Number of data sources. n.data <- 4 # Sites for each data source.  J.obs <- sample(ceiling(0.2 * J.all):ceiling(0.5 * J.all), n.data, replace = TRUE) # Replicates for each data source. n.rep <- list() for (i in 1:n.data) {   n.rep[[i]] <- sample(1:4, size = J.obs[i], replace = TRUE) } # Occupancy covariates beta <- c(0.5, 1, -3) p.occ <- length(beta) # Detection covariates alpha <- list() for (i in 1:n.data) {   alpha[[i]] <- runif(sample(1:4, 1), -1, 1) } p.det.long <- sapply(alpha, length) p.det <- sum(p.det.long) sigma.sq <- 2 phi <- 3 / .5 sp <- TRUE  # Simulate occupancy data.  dat <- simIntOcc(n.data = n.data, J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, J.obs = J.obs,                   n.rep = n.rep, beta = beta, alpha = alpha, sp = TRUE,                   cov.model = 'gaussian', sigma.sq = sigma.sq, phi = phi)

code: J.x <- 8 J.y <- 8 J <- J.x * J.y n.rep <- sample(2:4, size = J, replace = TRUE) N <- 10 # Community-level covariate effects # Occurrence beta.mean <- c(0.2, -0.15) p.occ <- length(beta.mean) tau.sq.beta <- c(0.6, 0.3) # Detection alpha.mean <- c(0.5, 0.2) tau.sq.alpha <- c(0.2, 0.3) p.det <- length(alpha.mean) psi.RE <- list(levels = c(10),                 sigma.sq.psi = c(1.5)) p.RE <- list(levels = c(15),               sigma.sq.p = 0.8) # Draw species-level effects from community means. beta <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = p.occ) alpha <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = p.det) for (i in 1:p.occ) {   beta[, i] <- rnorm(N, beta.mean[i], sqrt(tau.sq.beta[i])) } for (i in 1:p.det) {   alpha[, i] <- rnorm(N, alpha.mean[i], sqrt(tau.sq.alpha[i])) } # Spatial parameters if desired phi <- runif(N, 3/1, 3/.1) sigma.sq <- runif(N, 0.3, 3) sp <- TRUE  dat <- simMsOcc(J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, n.rep = n.rep, N = N, beta = beta,                  alpha = alpha, psi.RE = psi.RE, p.RE = p.RE, sp = TRUE,                  cov.model = 'exponential', phi = phi, sigma.sq = sigma.sq)

title: Single-Species, Multi-Species, and Integrated Spatial Occupancy Models — spOccupancy-package
text: Fits single-species, multi-species, integrated non-spatial spatial  occupancy models using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). Models fit using  Polya-Gamma data augmentation detailed Polson, Scott, Windle (2013).  Spatial models fit using either Gaussian processes Nearest Neighbor  Gaussian Processes (NNGP) large spatial datasets. Details NNGPs  given Datta, Banerjee, Finley, Gelfand (2016). Provides functionality  data integration multiple single-species occupancy data sets using  joint likelihood framework. Details data integration given  Miller, Pacifici, Sanderlin, Reich (2019). Details single-species  multi-species models found MacKenzie et al. (2002) Dorazio Royle (2005),  respectively. Details package functionality given Doser et al. (2022)  Doser, Finley, Banerjee (2022). See citation('spOccupancy')  cite spOccupancy publications. Model Fitting Functions PGOcc fits single-species occupancy models. spPGOcc fits single-species spatial occupancy models. msPGOcc fits multi-species occupancy models. spMsPGOcc fits multi-species spatial occupancy models. intPGOcc fits single-species integrated occupancy models (.e., occupancy model multiple data sources). spIntPGOcc fits single-species integrated spatial occupancy models. lfJSDM fits joint species distribution model without imperfect detection. sfJSDM fits spatial joint species distribution model without imperfect detection. lfMsPGOcc fits joint species distribution model imperfect detection (.e., multi-species occupancy model residual species correlations). sfMsPGOcc fits spatial joint species distribution model imperfect detection. tPGOcc fits multi-season single-species occupancy model. stPGOcc fits multi-season single-species spatial occupancy model. svcPGBinom fits single-species spatially-varying coefficient GLM. svcPGOcc fits single-species spatially-varying coefficient occupancy model. svcTPGBinom fits single-species spatially-varying coefficient multi-season GLM. svcTPGOcc fits single-species spatially-varying coefficient multi-season occupancy model. Goodness Fit Model Assessment Functions ppcOcc performs posterior predictive checks. waicOcc computes Widely Applicable Information Criterion spOccupancy model objects. Data Simulation Functions simOcc simulates single-species occupancy data. simTOcc simulates single-species multi-season occupancy data. simBinom simulates detection-nondetection data perfect detection. simTBinom simulates multi-season detection-nondetection data perfect detection. simMsOcc simulates multi-species occupancy data. simIntOcc simulates single-species occupancy data multiple data sources. objects model-fitting functions support summary function  displaying concise summary model results, fitted function extracting  model fitted values, predict function predicting occupancy /detection across area interest.

effects psi.RE <- list() # Spatial parameters sp <- TRUE # Two spatially-varying covariates.  svc.cols <- c(1, 2) p.svc <- length(svc.cols) cov.model <- "exponential" sigma.sq <- runif(p.svc, 0.4, 1.5) phi <- runif(p.svc, 3/1, 3/0.2)  # Simulate the data   dat <- simBinom(J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, weights = weights, beta = beta,                  psi.RE = psi.RE, sp = sp, svc.cols = svc.cols,                  cov.model = cov.model, sigma.sq = sigma.sq, phi = phi)  # Binomial data y <- dat$y # Covariates X <- dat$X # Spatial coordinates coords <- dat$coords  # Package all data into a list # Covariates covs <- cbind(X) colnames(covs) <- c('int', 'cov.1', 'cov.2', 'cov.3')  # Data list bundle data.list <- list(y = y,                    covs = covs,                   coords = coords,                    weights = weights) # Priors prior.list <- list(beta.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),                     sigma.sq.ig = list(a = 2, b = 1),                     phi.unif = list(a = 3 / 1, b = 3 / 0.1))   # Starting values inits.list <- list(beta = 0, alpha = 0,                    sigma.sq = 1, phi = phi) # Tuning tuning.list <- list(phi = 1)   n.batch <- 10 batch.length <- 25 n.burn <- 100 n.thin <- 1  out <- svcPGBinom(formula = ~ cov.1 + cov.2 + cov.3,                    svc.cols = c(1, 2),             data = data.list,              n.batch = n.batch,              batch.length = batch.length,              inits = inits.list,              priors = prior.list,             accept.rate = 0.43,              cov.model = "exponential",              tuning = tuning.list,              n.omp.threads = 1,              verbose = TRUE,              NNGP = TRUE,              n.neighbors = 5,             n.report = 2,              n.burn = n.burn,              n.thin = n.thin, code: set.seed(1000) # Sites J.x <- 15 J.y <- 15  J <- J.x * J.y # Years sampled n.time <- sample(10, J, replace = TRUE) # Binomial weights weights <- matrix(NA, J, max(n.time)) for (j in 1:J) {   weights[j, 1:n.time[j]] <- sample(5, n.time[j], replace = TRUE) } # Occurrence -------------------------- beta <- c(-2, -0.5, -0.2, 0.75) p.occ <- length(beta) trend <- TRUE sp.only <- 0 psi.RE <- list() # Spatial parameters ------------------ sp <- TRUE svc.cols <- c(1, 2, 3) p.svc <- length(svc.cols) cov.model <- "exponential" sigma.sq <- runif(p.svc, 0.1, 1) phi <- runif(p.svc, 3/1, 3/0.2) # Temporal parameters ----------------- ar1 <- TRUE  rho <- 0.8 sigma.sq.t <- 1  # Get all the data dat <- simTBinom(J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, n.time = n.time, weights = weights, beta = beta,                   psi.RE = psi.RE, sp.only = sp.only, trend = trend,                   sp = sp, svc.cols = svc.cols,                   cov.model = cov.model, sigma.sq = sigma.sq, phi = phi,                  rho = rho, sigma.sq.t = sigma.sq.t, ar1 = TRUE, x.positive = FALSE)  # Prep the data for spOccupancy ------------------------------------------- y <- dat$y X <- dat$X X.re <- dat$X.re coords <- dat$coords  # Package all data into a list covs <- list(int = X[, , 1],              trend = X[, , 2],              cov.1 = X[, , 3],               cov.2 = X[, , 4]) # Data list bundle data.list <- list(y = y,                   covs = covs,                   weights = weights,                    coords = coords) # Priors prior.list <- list(beta.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),                    sigma.sq.ig = list(a = 2, b = 1),                    phi.unif = list(a = 3/1, b = 3/.1),                     sigma.sq.t.ig = c(2, 0.5),                     rho.unif = c(-1, 1))  # Starting values inits.list <- list(beta = beta, alpha = 0,                    sigma.sq = 1, phi = 3 / 0.5,                     sigma.sq.t = 0.5, rho = 0) # Tuning tuning.list <- list(phi = 0.4, nu = 0.3, rho = 0.2)  # MCMC settings n.batch <- 2 n.burn <- 0 n.thin <- 1  out <- svcTPGBinom(formula = ~ trend + cov.1 + cov.2,                     svc.cols = svc.cols,                    data = data.list,                     n.batch = n.batch,                     batch.length = 25,                     inits = inits.list,                     priors = prior.list,                    accept.rate = 0.43,                     cov.model = "exponential",                     ar1 = TRUE,                    tuning = tuning.list,                     n.omp.threads = 1,                     verbose = TRUE,                     NNGP = TRUE,                     n.neighbors = 5,                    n.report = 1,                     n.burn = n.burn,                     n.thin = n.thin,                     n.chains = 1)  #> (j in 1:J) {   n.rep[j, 1:n.time[j]] <- sample(4, n.time[j], replace = TRUE) } # Occurrence -------------------------- beta <- c(-2, -0.5, -0.2, 0.75) trend <- TRUE  sp.only <- 0 psi.RE <- list() # Detection --------------------------- alpha <- c(1, 0.7, -0.5) p.RE <- list() # Spatial parameters ------------------ sp <- TRUE svc.cols <- c(1, 2, 3) p.svc <- length(svc.cols) cov.model <- "exponential" sigma.sq <- runif(p.svc, 0.1, 1) phi <- runif(p.svc, 3 / 1, 3 / 0.2) rho <- 0.8 sigma.sq.t <- 1 ar1 <- TRUE    x.positive <- FALSE   # Get all the data dat <- simTOcc(J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, n.time = n.time, n.rep = n.rep,                 beta = beta, alpha = alpha, sp.only = sp.only, trend = trend,                 psi.RE = psi.RE, p.RE = p.RE,                 sp = sp, cov.model = cov.model, sigma.sq = sigma.sq, phi = phi,                 svc.cols = svc.cols, ar1 = ar1, rho = rho, sigma.sq.t = sigma.sq.t,                 x.positive = x.positive)  # Data summary ------------------------------------------------------------ apply(dat$psi, 2, mean) #>  [1] 0.3269073 0.4299322 0.4184821 0.4536458 0.3235962 0.3652953 0.4298863 #>  [8] 0.1850842 0.2898164 0.2206873  # Prep the data for svcTPGOcc --------------------------------------------- # Full data set  y <- dat$y X <- dat$X X.re <- dat$X.re X.p <- dat$X.p X.p.re <- dat$X.p.re coords <- dat$coords  # Package all data into a list occ.covs <- list(int = X[, , 1],                   trend = X[, , 2],                   occ.cov.1 = X[, , 3],                   occ.cov.2 = X[, , 4])  # Detection det.covs <- list(det.cov.1 = X.p[, , , 2],                   det.cov.2 = X.p[, , , 3])  # Data list bundle data.list <- list(y = y,                    occ.covs = occ.covs,                   det.covs = det.covs,                    coords = coords) # Priors prior.list <- list(beta.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),                     alpha.normal = list(mean = 0, var = 2.72),                    phi.unif = code: set.seed(400) # Simulate Data ----------------------------------------------------------- J.x <- 8 J.y <- 8 J <- J.x * J.y n.rep <- sample(2:4, J, replace = TRUE) beta <- c(0.5, -0.15) p.occ <- length(beta) alpha <- c(0.7, 0.4) p.det <- length(alpha) dat <- simOcc(J.x = J.x, J.y = J.y, n.rep = n.rep, beta = beta, alpha = alpha,               sp = FALSE) occ.covs <- dat$X[, 2, drop = FALSE] colnames(occ.covs) <- c('occ.cov') det.covs <- list(det.cov = dat$X.p[, , 2]) # Data bundle data.list <- list(y = dat$y,                   occ.covs = occ.covs,                   det.covs = det.covs)  # Priors prior.list <- list(beta.normal = list(mean = rep(0, p.occ),                                       var = rep(2.72, p.occ)),                    alpha.normal = list(mean = rep(0, p.det),                                        var = rep(2.72, p.det))) # Initial values inits.list <- list(alpha = rep(0, p.det),                    beta = rep(0, p.occ),                    z = apply(data.list$y, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE))  n.samples <- 5000 n.report <- 1000  out <- PGOcc(occ.formula = ~ occ.cov,              det.formula = ~ det.cov,              data = data.list,              inits = inits.list,              n.samples = n.samples,              priors = prior.list,              n.omp.threads = 1,              verbose = TRUE,              n.report = n.report,               n.burn = 4000,               n.thin = 1) #> ---------------------------------------- #> 	Preparing to run the model #> ---------------------------------------- #> ---------------------------------------- #> 	Model description #> ---------------------------------------- #> Occupancy model with Polya-Gamma latent #> variable fit with 64 sites. #>  #> Samples per Chain: 5000  #> Burn-in: 4000  #> Thinning Rate: 1  #> Number of Chains: 1  #> Total Posterior Samples: 1000  #>  #>  #> Source compiled with OpenMP support and model fit using 1 thread(s). #>  #> ---------------------------------------- #> 	Chain 1 #> ---------------------------------------- #> Sampling ...  #> Sampled: 1000 of 5000, 20.00% #> ------------------------------------------------- #> Sampled: 2000 of 5000, 40.00% #> ------------------------------------------------- #> Sampled: 3000 of 5000, 60.00% #> ------------------------------------------------- #> Sampled: 4000 of 5000, 80.00% #> ------------------------------------------------- #> Sampled: 5000 of 5000, 100.00%  #
